items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: I had played in his church once, if not twice

ctx.x: I got this white boy, and everything was going smooth and so we were in Jacksonville, Florida and I had another young man that I got, a negro out of Seattle, Washington, Muse was his name, he was a tenor player, Muse, and he was a little different from we midwest southerners; in other words, he was regular and all, but you know, we have this habit of huddling. You see one negro in a public place we all get together; and so anyway, we were in Jacksonville, Florida at the top of the peninsula, so I decided I'd talk…

So he checked us in after the dance, we were doing a concert there, and a Reverend King, a Methodist preacher, they change at certain times, and I had played in his church once, if not twice, on Mother's Day and they later transferred him to Jacksonville and so he
saw where we were playing there and from Oklahoma, he just says well I got to go speak to him anyway.
